description: Add a first-class Uninstall action so a founder can fully remove a managed app from HomeBase without shell cleanup, stale reinstall blockers, or hidden retained restore state. The UI language should use 'Uninstall' consistently, and once an app is uninstalled it should return to the same product state as an app that is merely available to install.

timing.plannedEarliestExecution: After admin auth and core install/backup/restore flows are stable enough to support a destructive inverse operation
timing.gatingCondition: Requires admin-guarded destructive execution, trustworthy app metadata, and a clear decision on what artifacts are removed by default.

principles: Use the word 'Uninstall' in the UI; do not use 'Decommission'
Uninstall is destructive and must require an explicit extra confirmation
Once uninstalled, the app should behave as fully removed from HomeBase
A just-uninstalled app returns to the same visible state as any app that is simply available to install
Do not create surprise retained backups; preserving backups must be an explicit founder choice
Do not require or prompt for a fresh backup before uninstall; the founder may optionally keep existing backups
If backup preservation is offered, it should be a clear 'Keep backups' toggle that defaults ON

techStack.runtime: systemd, nginx, git checkout cleanup, filesystem deletion, optional PostgreSQL/database teardown
techStack.storage: SQLite installations/jobs/backup records plus app-specific runtime assets
techStack.testing: Planner tests, dry-run endpoint tests, UI source assertions, manual VM uninstall/reinstall rehearsal

userStories.title: Founder can see and understand a destructive Uninstall action
acceptanceCriteria: Installed app detail presents an Uninstall action using that exact word
Uninstall is clearly marked destructive and requires admin unlock plus an extra explicit confirmation

The confirmation explains at a high level what will be removed: service/runtime wiring, install files, app state tracked by HomeBase, and that the 'Keep backups' toggle controls whether local backup archives are preserved
Uninstall is not available for apps that are not currently installed
The Uninstall UI includes a 'Keep backups' toggle that defaults ON
userStories.testStrategy: UI source assertions plus endpoint auth/confirm tests

userStories.title: Uninstall removes the app from HomeBase-managed state
acceptanceCriteria: Execution stops and disables the app service/timers when applicable
Execution removes HomeBase-managed nginx/service/config/install artifacts for that app
Execution removes the app's installation record and backup records from HomeBase state so the app no longer appears as installed
If the founder leaves Keep backups enabled, backup archive files remain in place under the existing app backup root while install state is removed from HomeBase
After success, the app appears on the Apps page only under Available to install
A second uninstall attempt is blocked or reported as already uninstalled rather than failing messily
userStories.testStrategy: Planner tests, state transition tests, and manual VM uninstall/reinstall pass

userStories.title: Uninstall leaves the system in a clean reinstallable state
acceptanceCriteria: After uninstall, reinstalling the same app from HomeBase does not require manual shell cleanup
No stale systemd unit, nginx snippet, install directory, or HomeBase state record blocks reinstall
Job detail makes the uninstall steps and final result auditable
Dry-run shows the full uninstall plan before execution
userStories.testStrategy: Dry-run endpoint tests plus manual VM uninstall-then-reinstall rehearsal

high: If uninstall leaves hidden state behind, HomeBase will give false confidence that the app is truly gone
Deleting backups is destructive and preserving backups changes later restore semantics, so the toggle behavior must be clearly communicated before execution
Database/file removal differs across apps and can create partial uninstall failures if contracts are inconsistent
medium: Some apps may have extra timers, sidecars, or data directories beyond the current manifest surface
Preserved on-disk backups may reappear after reinstall through disk discovery, which is acceptable if the UI explains it
Failure halfway through uninstall can leave the app neither clearly installed nor clearly removed
A founder may misread the 'Keep backups' toggle unless the default and consequences are explicit
low: The first version can target HomeBase-managed artifacts only and document any unsupported app-specific leftovers that emerge during rehearsal

preFlightChecklist: Define the default removal set precisely: install dir, config/env files, systemd units, nginx snippets, database, backup artifacts, SQLite backup records
Define the exact 'Keep backups' semantics; default is ON
Keep backups leaves archive files in place under the existing backup root in v1; do not invent a new quarantine location yet
Align uninstall gating with current destructive-job behavior; current HomeBase execute endpoints do not generally block on unrelated running jobs
Set 'Keep backups' toggle default to ON without requiring or prompting for a fresh backup before uninstall
Choose the confirmation UX pattern for a destructive irreversible action on mobile and desktop
